reason: Ti substitution is the more physically credible intervention because Ti is already compatible with the alloy’s BCC refractory solid solution, whereas calling low-melting Sc refractory and assuming it will preserve strength near 1000 °C are poorly justified. B remains imperfect—its 10–20% density estimate is weakly supported and its rejection rule should explicitly require a density decrease—but it offers the sounder, more testable proposal overall.
